quarterly_data.signal: Northrop Grumman 10-K (fiscal 2025): total sales $41,954 million (2025 sales increased $921 million, or 2 percent); segment sales Aeronautics Systems $12,992 million, Defense Systems $8,002 million, Mission Systems $12,506 million, Space Systems $10,771 million. 2025 net awards totaled $46.3 billion; significant new awards include $14.8 billion for restricted programs, $3.3 billion for F-35, $2.5 billion for GEM 63, $1.8 billion for GWS and $1.3 billion for Virginia Class submarines. Total backlog was $95.7 billion versus $91.5 billion at December 31, 2024 ($43,529 million funded); approximately 35 percent is expected to be recognized as revenue over the next 12 months and 60 percent over the next 24 months. International sales were $5,990 million (14 percent) and fixed-price contracts were 50 percent of sales.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 sales $41,954 million (+2 percent); net awards $46.3 billion; GEM 63 awards $2.5 billion; backlog $95.7 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Northrop Grumman 10-K: Space Systems 2025 sales decreased $960 million, or 8 percent, to $10,771 million, mainly from the wind-down of the restricted space and NGI programs (-$738 million), a $172 million decrease for the SDA satellite programs due to the timing of materials and a $102 million decrease on the SLS Booster program; operating income was $1,183 million at an 11.0 percent margin. Approximately 45 percent of Space Systems is performed through restricted programs; its key programs also include the SDA Tracking and Transport layers, the Glide Phase Interceptor (GPI), Cygnus for NASA Commercial Resupply Services, Missile Defense Agency GWS interceptors and boosters, the HALO module for NASA's Lunar Gateway, Next-Gen OPIR satellites and payloads, SLS solid rocket motors and Trident II medium-class solid rocket motors.
quarterly_data.figure: Space Systems 2025 sales $10,771 million (-8 percent); operating margin 11.0 percent; about 45 percent restricted

quarterly_data.signal: Northrop Grumman 10-K on the B-21: the 2015 U.S. Air Force contract covers EMD plus five low-rate initial production (LRIP) options for a baseline total of 21 aircraft, with not-to-exceed pricing for additional aircraft up to unit 40; Northrop recognized a projected loss of $1.56 billion across the five LRIP options in Q4 2023 and an additional $477 million in Q1 2025, leaving a remaining loss accrual of $1.3 billion at December 31, 2025. It was in discussions with the Air Force on an accelerated production rate, which it expected would require future company investment to expand production capacity along with the opportunity to earn improved returns. Sentinel: the U.S. Air Force awarded a $13.3 billion EMD contract in 2020; after the Nunn-McCurdy review the DoW directed a restructure, and Northrop recognized a $76 million favorable EAC adjustment in Q2 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: B-21 baseline 21 aircraft; remaining loss accrual $1.3 billion; Sentinel EMD $13.3 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Northrop Grumman 10-K: 2025 capital expenditures were $1,450 million (Space Systems $403 million); at December 31, 2025 it had capital expenditure commitments of $1.6 billion and $23.9 billion of purchase obligations, largely open purchase order commitments to suppliers and subcontractors under U.S. government contracts. Company-sponsored IR&D was $1.1 billion (2.6 percent of sales). It had approximately 95,000 employees (about 7,500 hired in 2025) and approximately 53 million square feet of floor space at 446 locations. It has experienced challenges accessing certain raw materials due to inflation, geopolitical conflicts and microelectronics shortages, which have not, to date, materially impacted its ability to perform on its contracts.
quarterly_data.figure: capex $1,450 million; purchase obligations $23.9 billion; approximately 95,000 employees
